items.followUp: State the associative law for multiplication and give an example.

rubric.why: The definition must explain that changing the grouping leaves the result unchanged.
rubric.description: Defines the effect of regrouping operands.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that changing the grouping of operands does not change the result.

rubric.why: An associative-law equation demonstrates the definition.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example for addition or multiplication.

modelAnswer: The Associative Law states that changing the grouping of operands does not change the result.
For example, (a + b) + c = a + (b + c).

rubric.why: A bus topology uses one shared main cable.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that devices share one main or backbone cable.

rubric.why: The defining arrangement is that all computers connect to the shared cable.
rubric.description: Describes how devices connect in the topology.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that computers or devices connect to the same cable.

modelAnswer: In Bus Topology, all computers or devices are connected to a single main cable called the bus or backbone.
Data travels along this shared cable to the connected devices.

items.followUp: What is the use of POP3 protocol?

rubric.why: SMTP is used for sending email.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying that SMTP sends email messages.

rubric.why: SMTP is used to send email through mail servers, including between servers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning sending email to or between mail servers.

modelAnswer: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) is used to send email messages.
It transfers outgoing email from a user's device to a mail server and between mail servers.

items.followUp: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of star topology.

rubric.why: A central connecting device is the defining component of star topology.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a hub or switch is placed at the centre.

rubric.why: Each computer connects independently to the central device.
rubric.description: Describes the connections from the central device.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that every computer is connected to the hub or switch by its own cable.

modelAnswer: Place a central hub or switch in the network.
Connect each computer or device directly to the hub or switch using a separate cable.

items.followUp: Give one weakness of a transposition cipher.

rubric.why: A substitution cipher consistently replaces a plaintext letter with the same ciphertext letter.
rubric.description: Identifies the fixed letter replacement weakness.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that each plaintext letter is always replaced by the same letter or symbol.

rubric.why: The preserved letter frequencies make this cipher vulnerable to statistical analysis.
rubric.description: Explains how the cipher can be attacked.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that letter-frequency analysis can be used to break the cipher.

modelAnswer: Each plaintext letter is always replaced by the same ciphertext letter, so repeated-letter patterns are preserved.
The original message can be uncovered using letter-frequency analysis.

items.followUp: What is a strong password, and why should it be kept private?

rubric.why: Phishing involves deceptive messages or websites that impersonate trustworthy sources.
rubric.description: Identifies the deceptive means used in phishing.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing a fake email, message, or website.

rubric.why: Phishing attempts to steal sensitive information from its target.
rubric.description: States the information phishing tries to obtain.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying sensitive information, such as passwords or bank details, as the target.

modelAnswer: Phishing is a cyberattack in which an attacker uses fake emails, messages, or websites to deceive people.
The aim is to steal sensitive information such as passwords or bank details.

items.followUp: Write HTML code to make the word "Computer" bold.

rubric.why: The word must be enclosed in a valid HTML tag that displays it in italics.
rubric.description: Writes the correct italic HTML element and content.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for correctly enclosing Pakistan in an italic or emphasis tag.

items.followUp: Write an HTML font-tag example that changes text colour.

rubric.why: A font element must enclose text to apply formatting to it.
rubric.description: Uses opening and closing font tags around text.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly enclosing text within font tags.

rubric.why: The example should use a font attribute to format the enclosed text.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for including a font attribute such as color, size, or face.
